newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME Zinc at five-month high in Asia on Soros talk.
newsitem.headline: LME Zinc at five-month high in Asia on Soros talk.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three month zinc rose to a five-month high in Asian trading time on Thursday stoked by rumours that famed financier George Soros was making a speculative play in the market, traders said.

Zinc prices have rallied strongly in London this week on market talk that a large, losing long position once held by Spanish producer Asturiana de Zinc had been liquidated or transferred and that Soros had bought zinc or zinc-related equities.
Three month zinc was quoted at US$1,064/$1,069 a tonne at 0715 GMT compared with Wednesday's LME close at $1,054.
Japanese traders were generally positive on the zinc market's outlook, especially for the longer term, following Wednesday's rally on the LME.
A trader at a large Japanese trade house said that, while the latest gains seemed to be linked to the Asturiana and Soros rumours, a strong fundamental outlook should buoy the market.

In the near-term, he expected three-month zinc to hold above support at $1,040 a tonne, although prices would not receive much of lift from physical market activity in Japan and Southeast Asia, where inventories were plentiful and demand relatively modest.
"Last year and in the first half of this year the economies were strong and they (users) overestimated what they'd need," he said. "Inventories became excessive."

At the same time, he doubted that large amounts of spot sales would emerge from China following the recent rise in prices, partly because much of that country's production was tied up in long-term contracts.
For the longer term, however, he expected demand in the Far East to strengthen and predicted LME prices could breach $1,200 next year.
"Supplies cannot quickly increase and demand will be going strong," he said.

A source from another major Japanese trading house added, however, that several uncertainties still confront the zinc market, including the fate of Australia's A$1 billion Century zinc mine project, owned by CRA Ltd/RTZ Plc, that has been delayed by a native title dispute.
Singapore dealers were sceptical of the Soros rumours.

"People have been talking about this (Soros). Nobody knows why. There is basically no fundamental (reason) to support (zinc's current price)," Vinod Kumar, director of Singapore-based metal company Donald Mcarthy, told Reuters.
"Zinc should be at the $1,000 level," Kumar added.

A dealer at a Western metal trading house said funds had pushed zinc up on the back of the rumour, but added the availability of ample supplies of the metal should trim the price in the next few weeks.
"I think prices will drift back to $1,030 (a tonne). This has been more of a technical runup," he said.
But a trader in a major Japanese house, while discounting the Soros rumours, said zinc should consolidate its recent gains because demand is picking up.
"The demand for zinc is getting stronger and that should support the price more than the rumour about Soros going into Asturiana," the trader said.
